guidance: Some of the signs of that are evident in the developments in the transmission and renewable sector, increasing the earlier 500-gigawatt nonfossil capacity target to 900 gigawatts in the master plan.
Phase 2 target is set at INR16.72 lakh crores, and power sector allocation is about INR2.77 lakh crores for brownfield asset monetization.
capex: Both projects put together have approximately cumulative capex of INR5,800 crores.
As you can see in quarter 1 FY26 and quarter 1 FY27, there is a 12.5% growth of peak capacity, which is a significant growth by any standards on such a large portfolio.
risks: RE ambitions will drive growth, but with challenges; while renewable energy additions remain structurally strong and competitive, I do see near-term execution to face bottlenecks considering the transmission congestion,
So I think on the collection front, we are not seeing any challenge whatsoever.
focus: We focus on a business model with long-term contracts, low operating risk, and stable cash flows.
We focus on delivering a quarterly predictable distribution to our unitholders.
And while doing all this, we focus on an optimal cap structure.

about: India Grid Trust (IndiGrid) is the India's first listed power sector infrastructure investment trust, sponsored by KKR and Sterlite Power. It was established in 2016 to own and operate power transmission and renewable energy assets in India. [1] The Trust primarily acquires operational transmission SPVs (Special Purpose Vehicles) from a Sponsor or from a third party. [2] The entity is not a public/ private company. I
